A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 30 pages of v3 and 25 pages of v4, including appendices, were readable. Renumbered sections, tables and relocated figures could be matched reliably.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 classification experiments, hyperparameter studies and privacy-bound calculations.

after.justification: v4 retains the original empirical results and adds the feature-normalization experiment reported in Appendix D.1 and Table 2.

M1.justification: v4 adds a feature-normalized training variant with learning rates restricted by the smoothness bound (Appendix D.1). This is a limited procedural adaptation; the random-hyperplane construction, convex objective, optimizer updates and inference formula remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, FashionMNIST and CIFAR-10 classification. The added normalization experiment uses retained datasets and tasks; its preprocessing changes belong to the experimental protocol.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain DP-SGD with ReLU and convex models, logistic regression, and the three SSP feature variants. The new normalized-feature comparison reuses existing iterative comparators. Its reference to SSP does not establish a new SSP evaluation under normalization.

E3.justification: New Appendix D.1 specifies feature norm 5, clipping constant 10, P=64, and a NoisyCGD learning-rate grid restricted by η<2/(β+λ), retaining 400 epochs. Separately, SSP's reported MNIST/FashionMNIST feature count changes from 100 in v3 Appendix G.1 to 64 in v4 Appendix H.1. Unchanged SSP scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a focused check of accuracy when normalization and admissible learning rates enforce the privacy analysis's condition. The existing hyperplane-count studies, batch-size ablations and shuffling-bound analysis are retained.

E5.justification: The five-trial averages, 1.96-times-standard-error figure bars and three-run batch-size ablations are retained. New Table 2 also reports five-restart means with uncertainty values; no changed uncertainty procedure or increased repeat count is stated.

E6.justification: Original Table 1, v3 Table 2 (v4 Table 3), and all nine figures retain their results. New Table 2 reports normalized-feature NoisyCGD accuracies of 91.0/93.2% on MNIST and 41.7/45.0% on CIFAR-10 at ε=1.33/4.76. These are additional results under different preprocessing, not same-setting gains. Section 5 also corrects the noise-to-privacy-parameter pairing.

T1.justification: Lemma 3.1 replaces β=||x_j||²+λ with a bound containing the number of active hyperplanes, bounded by P. v3 Appendix C's block-diagonal Hessian argument is replaced by a rank-one Hessian proof in v4 Appendix D. New derivations cover multiclass cross-entropy, concentration of activation counts and feature scaling. These materially revise the mathematics supporting the privacy analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the claims of a strongly convex ReLU approximation, applicability of hidden-state privacy analysis, comparable privacy-utility trade-offs and a random-data utility analysis.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly acknowledges that the retained NoisyCGD experiments assume a required learning-rate/smoothness condition without enforcing it, substantially qualifying their privacy interpretation. Appendix D explains normalization as a remedy. Remark 1 expands the random-data applicability discussion, while new Appendix B identifies unresolved risks to minority-group accuracy.

D1.justification: v4 clarifies noise-multiplier versus raw-noise conventions and supplies normalization, clipping, hyperplane-count and learning-rate instructions for the new experiment. It revises SSP feature counts and removes the explicit statement that logistic regression uses the same private hyperparameter-tuning procedure as the proposed method.

R1.justification: v4 adds Farrand et al. (2020) and Bagdasaryan et al. (2019) on differential privacy and fairness. It also expands comparison with the already-cited Brown et al. (2024), emphasizing feature-dimension dependence and label assumptions. The central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 copyedits the prose, clarifies the convex-reformulation explanation, and reorganizes the notation glossary. The main section sequence and contribution narrative remain stable; appendix lettering changes largely follow the insertion of the broader-impact statement.

P2.justification: v4 adopts NeurIPS formatting, substantially changing typography, title design, margins, table styling and figure placement. Figures 2 and 3 now share a page, and other plots are resized or relocated. A new Table 2 is inserted, while the former Table 2 becomes Table 3.

improvement.justification: v3's smoothness bound omitted the active-hyperplane factor, compromising the justification for applying the NoisyCGD privacy theorem. v4 corrects the proof, discloses the unenforced condition in the retained experiments, and adds a normalized-feature experiment with restricted learning rates. These substantially improve correctness, transparency and empirical support, although they do not retrospectively validate the privacy guarantees of the retained NoisyCGD results.
